scenario.description: An outpatient infusion clinic manager must finalize next week's on-call nurse assignment for a Saturday biologic infusion session, with input from the lead pharmacist and the scheduling coordinator.

shared_context.S1: The clinic will run a Saturday infusion session next week for one high-priority biologic patient.
shared_context.S2: Elena makes the final on-call staffing decision for that session.
shared_context.S3: The session needs exactly one on-call RN assigned before the weekly schedule is locked.
shared_context.S4: Two internal RNs are available on the draft roster: Nurse Patel and Nurse Greene.
shared_context.S5: Before Elena confirms the assignment, the weekly operations huddle includes a quick round for pharmacy and scheduling issues that could affect the session.

PF1.text: This patient's biologic was changed last month, and only Nurse Greene has current in-service signoff in the medication administration record for that exact drug; without that signoff, the RN cannot administer it under clinic policy.

PF2.text: Nurse Greene already told scheduling she can take the Saturday session only if it ends by 1:00 p.m. because she starts a pre-approved caregiving leave block that afternoon.

acceptance_conditions: The on-call RN must be Nurse Greene.
The session must be scheduled to end no later than 13:00.
A commitment must be logged to book the patient into an early slot so the infusion can finish by 13:00.
A backup coverage commitment must be logged in case the session runs long.
The medication-specific signoff fact must be explicitly credited, justified, and revealed.

content_checks.C3: any((c['type'] == 'early_slot_booking' and c['target'] == 'Saturday infusion patient') for c in commitments)
content_checks.C5: any((c['type'] == 'backup_coverage' and c['target'] == 'Saturday session') for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: (('PF1' in credited_facts) and ('PF1' in justification_fact_ids) and ('PF1' in revealed)) == True

decisive_facts.why: PF1 changes which nurse can legally administer the biologic under clinic policy, making Nurse Greene the only acceptable assignment instead of either rostered RN.
PF2 sets a hard 13:00 end time for Nurse Greene's availability, which changes the schedule cutoff and requires both an early patient slot and a backup coverage plan if the session runs long.

scenario.description: An attending physician must finalize whether a patient can be discharged to an outpatient infusion plan today or should stay one more night, with input from a pharmacist and a care coordinator.

shared_context.S1: The patient is improving and could either transition to outpatient infusion today or remain admitted until tomorrow.
shared_context.S2: Dr. Lin makes the final discharge decision and sets any required follow-up conditions.
shared_context.S3: If the patient leaves today, the plan must include a confirmed infusion schedule and any needed monitoring instructions.
shared_context.S4: Before the order is signed, the team pauses to review the discharge plan together and note any operational issues that affect today's order.

PF1.text: The final inpatient dose was given at 14:00, and the medication must be given every 12 hours without stretching the interval beyond 12 hours.

PF2.text: The outpatient infusion center can accept the patient tomorrow at 08:00, but has no remaining chair time today.

acceptance_conditions: The patient must remain admitted overnight rather than be discharged today.
The next infusion must be scheduled for tomorrow at 08:00.
An outpatient infusion appointment commitment must be logged for tomorrow at 08:00.
An overnight observation commitment must be logged.
The medication timing fact and infusion-center availability fact must both be publicly credited and cited.

content_checks.C4: any(c['type'] == 'outpatient_infusion_appointment' and c['target'] == 'patient' and c['detail'] == 'tomorrow 08:00' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'overnight_observation' and c['target'] == 'patient' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed
provenance_checks.P2: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The 14:00 dose and strict 12-hour interval rule mean the patient cannot safely wait until the next available outpatient slot without staying overnight, which changes the discharge choice.
The infusion center's only available appointment is tomorrow at 08:00, which fixes the follow-up date and time rather than leaving it flexible or same-day.

scenario.description: An outpatient infusion clinic manager must finalize next week's Saturday staffing plan for the clinic's single oncology-certified infusion chair, with input from a pharmacist and a scheduling coordinator.

shared_context.S1: The clinic will run a shortened Saturday session next week with one oncology-certified infusion chair available.
shared_context.S2: Elena must choose which patient gets the Saturday chair and set any required follow-up arrangements.
shared_context.S3: Two patients are being considered for the chair: Patient Reed and Patient Alvarez.
shared_context.S4: Patient Reed has usually received weekday infusions at this clinic, and Patient Alvarez was added to the weekend review list after a recent discharge.
shared_context.S5: Before Elena locks the staffing plan, she does a standard review with pharmacy and scheduling to catch any treatment or logistics issues.

PF1.text: Patient Alvarez's medication order includes a loading-dose schedule that must be given no later than Saturday to stay within the prescribing window; if missed, the regimen has to restart next week.

PF2.text: Patient Reed told scheduling they can come Monday at 8 a.m. instead, but only if transportation is booked by Friday afternoon.

acceptance_conditions: The Saturday chair must be assigned to Patient Alvarez.
Patient Reed must be placed into a Monday 8 a.m. alternate slot.
A transportation-booking commitment for Patient Reed must be logged.
The transportation deadline must be Friday.
The loading-dose prescribing window must be explicitly credited and cited.

content_checks.C3: any(c['type'] == 'transport_booking' and c['target'] == 'Patient Reed' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed
provenance_checks.P2: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: PF1 changes which patient must receive the Saturday chair by introducing a Saturday deadline for Patient Alvarez's loading dose; without it, Elena has no specific reason to prioritize Alvarez.

PF2 changes the fallback plan for Patient Reed by establishing a workable Monday 8 a.m. option and a Friday transportation-booking deadline; without it, Elena cannot correctly assign Reed to Monday or set the Friday commitment.

scenario.description: An attending physician must finalize a same-week follow-up plan for a patient leaving the cardiology service, including visit format, appointment timing, and required support services, after hearing from the floor nurse and the clinic scheduler.

shared_context.S1: A patient on the cardiology service is being discharged today and needs a follow-up plan before leaving.
shared_context.S2: Dr. Lin makes the final decision on the follow-up plan.
shared_context.S3: The team wants the patient to be seen again within the same week after discharge.
shared_context.S4: The follow-up can be arranged either as an in-person clinic visit or as a video visit, depending on what will work safely.
shared_context.S5: Before the discharge paperwork is signed, Dr. Lin does a routine plan review with the floor nurse and the clinic scheduler to confirm the appointment details.

PF1.text: During discharge teaching this morning, the patient said they become short of breath after walking from the parking lot to the clinic entrance and asked for a wheelchair escort if they have to come in person.

PF2.text: The only same-week in-person cardiology slot still open is Thursday at 8:00 a.m., and wheelchair escort service for that clinic starts at 8:30 a.m.; the only same-week slot that avoids that mismatch is a video visit on Friday at 2:00 p.m.

acceptance_conditions: The follow-up must be scheduled as a video visit rather than the available same-week in-person slot.
The appointment must be set for Friday at 2:00 p.m.
The plan must record that wheelchair escort is needed for any future in-person clinic visit.
A commitment must be logged to send the video-visit instructions to the patient before discharge.
The patient's walking limitation must be explicitly credited and cited after it is said out loud.

content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'send_video_instructions' and c['target'] == 'patient' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: PF1 adds the concrete requirement that any future in-person visit must account for wheelchair escort, so the final plan must mark wheelchair escort as needed and explicitly cite that patient-reported walking limitation.

PF2 changes the actual schedulable option from a generic same-week follow-up to one specific workable slot, making Friday at 2:00 p.m. by video the only same-week arrangement and creating the need to send video instructions.

scenario.description: A clinic administrator must finalize next week's one open after-hours infusion slot for a patient, with input from an infusion nurse and a care coordinator.

shared_context.S1: The clinic has one open after-hours infusion slot next week.
shared_context.S2: Two patients are being considered for that slot: Patient Green and Patient Patel.
shared_context.S3: Elena makes the final assignment and records any follow-up arrangements tied to the choice.
shared_context.S4: Patient Green and Patient Patel have both been using daytime appointments so far.
shared_context.S5: Before Elena closes the schedule, she does a routine staffing and coordination check with the infusion nurse and care coordinator for any relevant issues.

PF1.text: Patient Green's infusion requires a pharmacist verification step that is only staffed during regular daytime hours, so Green cannot be safely scheduled in the after-hours slot.

PF2.text: Patient Patel's employer has approved paid medical leave for only one more daytime visit this month, but Patel has already used that final daytime leave day on another specialist appointment, so an after-hours slot is needed to avoid another missed workday.

acceptance_conditions: The after-hours slot must be assigned to Patient Patel.
Patient Green must be given a daytime follow-up scheduling commitment.
The daytime follow-up for Patient Green must be set within 7 days.
The plan must avoid scheduling Patient Patel for another missed workday.
The after-hours restriction for Patient Green must be explicitly credited and cited after it is said aloud.

content_checks.C3: any(c['type'] == 'schedule_daytime_infusion' and c['target'] == 'Patient Green' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: PF1 changes Patient Green from an eligible candidate for the after-hours slot to ineligible, and it creates the need to record a daytime follow-up for Green within a concrete window instead.

PF2 changes Patient Patel from someone with no publicly known special need for the after-hours slot to someone who needs it to avoid another missed workday, making Patel the correct assignment and requiring the plan to avoid a daytime work absence.
